source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why does an action log separate a proposal, an attempt, and a verified result?

options.text: They establish different amounts of completion evidence.
options.feedback: A proposal describes intent, an attempt shows that an operation was tried, and a verified result shows the checked outcome. Keeping them distinct prevents an attempt from being reported as success.

options.text: Each is an interchangeable description of a completed operation.
options.feedback: These stages are not equivalent. A proposed or attempted repair can still fail to produce the required result.

options.text: A detailed proposal guarantees that the operation will execute properly.
options.feedback: A well-specified proposal can guide execution but cannot guarantee its result. The environment still has to be observed after acting.

options.text: Recording an attempted operation removes the need for later inspection.
options.feedback: A log of an attempt documents activity, not necessarily success. Verification needs evidence about the resulting object or behavior.
